name: LEANDER PAES
coach: N/A (Retired; formerly Rick Leach, Dave Rineberg)
bio:
Career Overview: Playing Style: A dynamic all-court player with exceptional reflexes and volleying skills, excelling in doubles with a quick serve and precise net play.
Career-High ATP Singles Ranking: #73 (August 24, 1998), Career-High ATP Doubles Ranking: #1 (June 21, 1999).
Best Grand Slam Singles Performance: Reached the third round of the 1997 US Open.
Grand Slam Achievements: Winner of 18 Grand Slam titles (8 men’s doubles, 10 mixed doubles), including a career Grand Slam in doubles (Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon, US Open).
Notable Achievements: Olympic Medal: Bronze medal in singles at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics, India’s first individual Olympic medal in decades. ATP Titles: Secured 1 singles title (1998 Newport) and 54 doubles titles. Davis Cup & National Representation: India’s most successful Davis Cup player with a record of 45-13 in doubles, competing from 1990 to 2019.
Other Highlights: Known for iconic partnerships with Mahesh Bhupathi (‘Indian Express’), Radek Štěpánek, and Martina Hingis. Retired in 2020 as one of the greatest doubles players in tennis history.
Paes left an indelible legacy in Indian tennis, inspiring generations with his longevity and success. 🎾🇮🇳
